                    ### Question
                    A 32-year-old woman comes to her doctor’s office with abdominal distention, diffuse abdominal pain, and a history of 10–12 bowel movements a day for the last week. She was diagnosed with Crohn’s disease 3 years ago. Today, vitals are normal. Her abdomen is mildly distended and diffusely tender to palpation. A CT scan shows evidence of a fistula and strictures located in the last 30 cm of her ileum. A resection of the affected portion of the bowel is scheduled. What changes in bile metabolism are expected in this patient post-procedure?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Absorption of vitamin K will not be impaired
opb. Synthesis of cholesterol in the liver will decrease
opc. The balance of the components in bile will be altered
opd. Enteric bacteria will remain the same in the small intestine
ope. Absorption of  7⍺-dehydroxylated bile will decrease

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
Resection of the ileum leads to decreased absorption of bile acids, which alters bile metabolism and changes the balance of bile components (CHAIN 1 and 3). Vitamin K absorption may be impaired due to the loss of ileal function, but this does not directly impact bile metabolism (CHAIN 2). The resection does not necessarily lead to a decrease in the synthesis of cholesterol in the liver (CHAIN 2 is incorrect). The absorption of 7α-dehydroxylated bile acids is expected to decrease due to reduced ileal absorption (CHAIN 4). Enteric bacteria may change post-resection, but the impact on bile metabolism is unclear (CHAIN 5). Therefore, the most relevant and supported options are that the balance of bile components will be altered and that absorption of 7α-dehydroxylated bile will decrease.
